description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—across a range of initial confidence values from 0.71 to 1.00. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” is linearly scaled with tick marks at intervals of approximately 0.02, ranging from 0.71 to 1.00. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” is also linear, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2. The blue solid line with circle markers represents “Final Accuracy,” which generally trends upward from ~0.90 at 0.71 initial confidence to a peak of ~0.95 near 0.79, then fluctuates between ~0.85 and 0.95 across higher confidence values, ending near 0.92 at 1.00. The green dashed line with square markers, “Initial Accuracy,” starts at ~0.55 at 0.71, rises to ~0.90 at 0.79, then dips and recovers, ending near 0.90 at 1.00. The orange dashed line with diamond markers, “Δ Accuracy” (change in accuracy), begins at ~0.38 at 0.71, drops sharply to near 0.0 at 0.73, rises to ~0.30 at 0.83, then declines again to near 0.0 at 0.90, with erratic fluctuations thereafter, ending near 0.08 at 1.00. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability in measurements, with larger error bars typically observed for Δ Accuracy at lower and mid-range confidence values.
